name: Maa Baulasuni Temple
significance: A Shakta shrine in the village of Nilok, about 27 km from Bhadrak town, where the goddess is venerated as a stone bearing a painted red face. The present temple dates from 1969 and its yagya mandap from 2000; the Makar Mela at Makar Sankranti is its principal gathering.
story: A Brahmin visitor is said to have seen children playing with a round stone under a tamarind tree, and after he and a villager both dreamt that Baulasuni dwelt there in the stone, the village began worshipping her as its protector.

name: Nandeeswarar Temple
deity: Shiva as Nandeeswarar, worshipped in the form of Nandi; goddess Aavudai Nayagi
builtDisplay: c. 11th c. (described as about 950 years old)
significance: A Shiva temple at Adambakkam in Chennai, near St Thomas Mount station, unusual in that the presiding form is Nandi standing before the sage Bringi rather than a linga. The article gives its age as roughly 950 years; a local attribution to a Chola patron is unverified.
story: Shiva is said to have appeared here to the sage Bringi in the form of Nandi, and the adjoining hill, once called Bringi Malai, came to be known as Parangi Malai.

name: Joy Dol (Keshavnarayan Vishnu Dol)
significance: A brick-and-stone Vishnu temple raised in 1698 by the Ahom king Rudra Singha on the bank of the Joysagar tank in memory of his mother Joymoti. Its walls carry carvings of celestial figures and of everyday Ahom life, and it stands with the Sivadol, Devi Ghar and Ghanashyam House as part of the Joysagar group.

name: Draupati Amman Temples, Kumbakonam
significance: A set of neighbourhood shrines to Draupati Amman spread across Kumbakonam, on the streets flanking the Chakrapani and Sarangapani temples and near the bus stand. Several also hold shrines to Vinayaka, Kali and Mariamman and sculpted heads of Aravan; their recorded consecrations fall between 2001 and 2016.

name: Parvati Temple, Bhubaneswar
significance: A small grey-sandstone shrine to Parvati in the old town of Bhubaneswar, near the Lingaraja temple, built in dry masonry and dated by its materials to the 14th century. Its pidha deul with a porch carries Dravidian decorative elements alongside the local Kalinga idiom.

name: Sree Narayanapuram Thrikkayil Temple
deity: Vishnu, in the four-armed form of Krishna
significance: One of the older temples of Perissery in Alappuzha district, where Vishnu is worshipped as a four-armed Krishna bearing conch, discus, mace and lotus and adorned with tulsi garlands. Its main observance is the twelve-lamp festival.

name: Prasanna Venkateswara Temple, Appalayagunta
significance: A Venkateswara temple near Tirupati completed in 1232 under Venkata Perumalaraju Brahmadeva of Karvetinagaram, where the deity's right hand is held in abhaya rather than the pose usual at Venkateswara shrines. It has been administered by the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams since 1988.

name: Dibbesvara Temple
significance: An early-medieval Shiva temple at Saripalli in Vizianagaram district, protected by the Archaeological Survey of India as a monument of national importance. Its square sanctum and tiered curvilinear shikhara follow the Kalinga rekha deul type, evidence of building contact between coastal Andhra and Odisha.

name: Bhimashankar Jyotirlinga (Dakinyam), Bhimpur
significance: A Shiva shrine at Bhimpur village on the Mahendratanaya river in the western Mahendragiri hills of Rayagada district, which came to notice when the site was excavated in 1974. The linga stands within a quadrangular Shakti and carries a sculpted sacred thread.
story: Citing the Linga Purana, local tradition holds this to be the jyotirlinga of the Dakini country, one of the twelve.

name: Chemmanthatta Mahadeva Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Chemmanthatta in Thrissur district counted among the 108 Shiva shrines of Kerala, with a gopuram rising about 33 m. The Archaeological Survey of India and the Kerala Ooralma Devaswom share responsibility for it.
story: Local tradition credits the sage Parashurama with installing the temple's idol.

name: Karppillikkavu Sree Mahadeva Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Manjapra in Ernakulam district where the deity is worshipped in his hunter form, Kirathamoorthy or Vettakkaran, and which is reckoned among the 108 major Shiva shrines. Its main festival runs eight days in the Malayalam month of Makaram.
story: The shrine is said to have first held an image of Devi, and Kartavirya Arjuna, finding her presence absent when he came for darshan, is held to have consecrated Shiva in her place.

name: Veerabhadreswarar Temple, Kumbakonam
deity: Shiva as Agora Veerabhadra, with the goddess Bhadrakali
significance: A west-facing Shiva temple in Kumbakonam whose presiding form is the fierce Agora Veerabhadra, paired with Bhadrakali. The Tamil poet Ottakoothar is said to have composed his Thakka Yaga Barani here.

name: Sri Krishnapuram Temple
deity: Krishna, with Shiva and the goddess worshipped in paired form
builtDisplay: Krishna deified 1078 ME; Shiva shrine 1124 ME
significance: A Krishna temple at Thalappalam near Erattupetta in Kottayam district, where Radha-Krishna and Parvati-Parameswara are venerated as paired deities. Long held by the Kochupurakkal Nair family, it later passed to the NSS Karayogam of Thalappalam.
story: Villagers tell of farmers whose iron tools struck something buried in the fields, revealing a divine presence, and the shrine was raised there in a season of famine and epidemic.

name: Bhagavadh Vinayaga Temple, Kumbakonam
significance: A Ganesha temple in Kumbakonam whose 1692 inscription records grants made under the Thanjavur Maratha rulers at the time of a renovation. It also holds a Navagraha Vinayaga, and at Vinayaka Chaturthi the deity is decorated with currency notes.
story: The site is said to have revealed itself when the ashes of the sage Bhagavar Maharishi's mother turned into flowers as they were immersed in the Kaveri here.

name: Chandikan Devi Temple (Chandikan Dham)
significance: A Kali shrine at Sandwa village, some 24 km from Pratapgarh town, around which a trading fair gathers every Tuesday. Its largest fair falls on Budhwa Mangal, and the Chandika Mahotsava is kept on the eighth and ninth days of Chaitra and Ashwin Navratri.

name: Puthoorppilly Sree Krishnaswamy Temple
significance: A Krishna temple at Manjapra in Ernakulam district, listed as a protected monument by the Kerala state archaeology department. Sreekrishna Jayanthi is its principal festival.

name: Shaktheeswaram Temple
significance: A Shakta temple at Aymanam near Kottayam whose presiding deity is Adi Parashakti, worshipped through Sri Chakra puja and tantric upasana. It is reached from Kottayam city by the Kudayampadi–Parippu road.

name: Chauharjan Devi Temple
significance: A shrine of the mother goddess Barahi, known locally as Chauharjan Devi, standing on the bank of the Sai river at Chauharjan Parasrampur in Pratapgarh district.

name: Koncheswar Mahadev Temple
significance: A brick Shiva temple at Konch in Gaya district, dated to about the 14th century, with a heavy curvilinear nagara sikhara over seven-faced outer walls. Cunningham and Beglar recorded it for the Archaeological Survey in 1872–73, when the tower still carried a cylindrical pinnacle; a Dashavatara panel and images of Vishnu, Hara-Gauri, Ganesha and Surya stand in the premises.

name: Akkanna Madanna Caves
style: Rock-cut, with early Nagara-rekha shikhara carving
significance: Rock-cut Shiva cave temples at Vijayawada excavated by the Eastern Chalukyas around the middle of the 7th century, the upper cave holding three shrines to different forms of Shiva and the lower caves showing experimental carving of a nagara-rekha superstructure. They are protected monuments of national importance, and take their present name from Akkanna and Madanna, ministers of Golconda a thousand years later.

name: Kapileshwar Temple, Madhubani
deity: Shiva (Kapileshwar linga), with Parvati and Hanuman
significance: One of the better-known Shiva temples of Madhubani district, set in a walled compound with subsidiary shrines and old sculptures. A large tank was dug beside it with help from the Darbhanga Raj to supply water for ritual, and in Shrawan pilgrims come from across Bihar for the jalabhishek of the linga.
story: The linga is said to have been installed here by the sage Kapila, from whom the temple takes its name.

name: Wangath Temple Complex, Naranag
builtDisplay: 8th c. (Lalitaditya Muktapida, Karkota); origin traced to c. 220 BCE
style: Kashmiri grey granite, with pyramidal roofs and domed ceilings
significance: A ruined group of Shaiva temples in grey granite beside the spring at Naranag in Ganderbal district, expanded in the 8th century under the Karkota ruler Lalitaditya Muktapida. Now centrally protected by the Archaeological Survey of India, the site is the starting point of the annual Gangbal yatra to Gangabal lake.
story: Kalhana's Rajatarangini credits King Jaluka, son of Ashoka, with raising the Bhuteshvara and Jyestarudra shrines here around 220 BCE.

name: Padiyanoor Devi Temple
deity: Chamundi Devi, a fierce form of Kali
significance: An old goddess temple at Poovachal, about 30 km from Thiruvananthapuram, where Chamundi is the cardinal deity and subsidiary shrines hold Yakshiyamma, Ganapati, Yogeshwara, Nagar and Brahmarakshas. Its three-day Makam Thozhal in Meenam is the year's main observance.

name: Dada Darbar, Khandwa
deity: Dadaji Dhuniwale — the samadhi of Shri 1008 Keshwanand ji Maharaj
significance: A shrine in Khandwa built over the samadhi of the Avadhoot saint Keshwanand ji Maharaj, known as Bade Dadaji or Dadaji Dhuniwale, who came here from Barwaha and took mahasamadhi on 3 December 1930. Twenty-seven further dhams of the same lineage exist in India and abroad.

name: Ootukulangara Bhagavathy Temple, Peruvemba
deity: Ootukulangara Bhagavathy, with Ganapathy and Ayyappan
significance: A Bhagavathy temple at Peruvemba in Palakkad district whose sanctum is left roofless, the idol standing under an asoka tree that is said never to have grown. Its main festival, Patham Padiyam, closes 41 days of lamp-lighting in the month of Vrischikam.
story: A farm worker is said to have turned up a metal image while ploughing a paddy field; an astrologer called in by the landlord judged it a self-manifested form of Bhagavathy, and the temple was raised on the spot.

name: Kalyana Venkateswara Temple, Srinivasamangapuram
significance: A Venkateswara temple at Srinivasamangapuram near Tirupati, listed by the Archaeological Survey of India as a monument of national importance and administered by the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams since 1981. Newly married couples come here for blessings.
story: Venkateswara is said to have spent the first six months after his marriage to Padmavathi at this place.

name: Kapalikulangara Sree Mahavishnu Temple
significance: A Mahavishnu temple at Taliparamba in Kannur district, built in the traditional Kerala manner and standing close to the Sree Rajarajeshwara temple.

name: Sri Ananda Lingeshwara Temple
builtDisplay: rebuilt 2000–2012; origin traced to the 13th c. Chola era
style: Modern Indian; the earlier Chola structure was demolished
significance: A Shiva temple on Ananda Giri hill near Hebbal in Bengaluru, traced in origin to the Chola period of the 13th century but rebuilt in successive renovations in 2000, 2009 and 2012. Maha Shivratri draws thousands to the hill.
story: Devotees first propitiate Kaala Bairaveshwara as guardian of the place, and a tunnel is said to have run from the hill to Nandi Hills for kings escaping attack.

name: Neendoor Subrahmanya Swami Temple
style: Traditional Kerala (laterite, terracotta tile and teak)
significance: A Murugan temple at Neendoor in Kottayam district, built of laterite and teak with carved woodwork throughout and a monolithic stone lamp, where the deity is worshipped in his fierce form as commander of the divine armies after the killing of Tharakasuran. It is said to be the only Subrahmanya temple performing the Ottanarangamala Samarppanam.
story: The Pandavas and the sage Vyasa are said to have worshipped at this temple.

name: Ashtabhuji Temple, Adbhar
deity: Ashtabhuji Devi, the eight-armed goddess identified with Saraswati and Durga
significance: A stone temple at Adbhar village in Janjgir-Champa district housing an eight-armed image of the goddess, built in the nagara manner during the Gupta period and since restored under the Archaeological Survey of India. Navratri is its chief festival.

name: Muthumariamman Temple, Tiruvappur
significance: A Mariamman temple at Tiruvappur in Thirukokarnam, about 5 km from Pudukkottai, where the goddess is enshrined seated behind a front mandapa, flagstaff and bali peetam. Its prakara also holds shrines to Meenakshi of Madurai and Kamatchi of Kanchipuram, and the Fridays of Aadi draw the largest crowds.
